title: Dan Dakich says Dabo Swinney is done at Clemson: 'No shot he wins (another) national championship'
text:
The OutKick host says Clemson's momentum has been gone for four or five years amid resistance to the transfer portal

Zero Shot Dabo Swinney Wins Another National Championship At Clemson | Don't @ Me w/ Dan Dakich

Dan Dakich doesn't see a world where Dabo Swinney lifts another National Championship while at the helm of the University of Clemson.

At the risk of sounding like a broken record, the clock may finally be striking midnight for Dabo Swinney's tenure as head coach of the Clemson Tigers.

Yes, bombard me with your "Groundhog's Day" memes all you want, but this cat may have finally run out of lives as the Clemson faithful may have also run out of patience.

His latest embarrassment, a 20-6 home loss to Georgia Tech, has fans and media members alike wondering if this might be it for the two-time national champion.

RANKING WHICH POWER 4 COLLEGE FOOTBALL HEAD COACHING JOB IS MOST LIKELY TO COME OPEN NEXT

Clemson Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney talks with the referee in the fourth quarter at Kenan Stadium on Oct. 4, 2025. (Bob Donnan/Imagn Images)

The Tigers don't even have a quarterback they can rely on, let alone a competent offense, and Swinney's resistance to using the transfer portal only continues to be magnified as teams like Wake Forest and SMU seem to be doing more with less resources.

I haven't exactly been shy in pointing this out for several months, and one man who is on board with the demise of Dabo at Clemson is none other than Dan Dakich.

CFP & ESPN INDIANA SLANDER CONTINUES, DAN DAKICH REACTS TO LATEST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RANKINGS - LISTEN NOW

Dakich took some time on his latest episode of "Don't @ Me" to take the Tigers legend to task over his latest failings.

"He may win a conference (title)," Dakich admits before pivoting to the hard truth. "But there is absolutely no shot he wins a national championship, and we can clip this."

THERE'S A DIFFERENCE BETWEEN COACHES WHO 'CAN'T' WIN A NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP AND COACHES WHO 'HAVEN'T'

Clemson Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney talks to an official during the NCAA football game against the Duke Blue Devils during the game at Memorial Stadium on Nov. 1, 2025. (Alex Martin/Imagn Images)

The outspoken OutKick host took things a step further, guaranteeing that Dabo wouldn't win another natty as long as he's still on the airwaves.

"I don't know how much time I got left," he said. "But he ain't winning one in the time I'm going to be on TV."

Brutal, but Dakich has a point.

Everything that Swinney has done since the advent of NIL and the transfer portal suggests that his program is moving in the opposite direction.

TRANSFER PORTAL, NOT NIL, REASON FOR PARITY, CLAIMS COLLEGE FOOTBALL EXPERT BROOKS AUSTIN

Clemson was the ACC in the mid-to-late 2010s.

After COVID, however, the Tigers started to fall behind, leaving a power vacuum in the conference that was eventually filled by Miami.

Now the Canes are the top dog, utilizing a mix of high school recruiting and supplementing with the transfer portal, something Dabo desperately needed to utilize while Clemson was still on top.

Miami Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal reacts after a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Panthers during the third quarter at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, on Nov. 29, 2025. (Charles LeClaire/Imagn Images)

The time to course correct may have already passed, though, as Dakich points out.

HOW MUCH LONGER DOES CLEMSON HEAD COACH DABO SWINNEY REALISTICALLY HAVE IN DEATH VALLEY?

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"When you lose momentum in your program, it is incredibly difficult to get back," Dakich surmises. "And this isn't just this year, this isn't just last year. It's been about four or five years."

"He may be the greatest coach on earth, but the momentum is gone."

That may be a tough pill to swallow for Clemson fans, but it's the truth.

And, in all honesty, it's a pill they may have been slowly swallowing for quite some time now.

Austin Perry is a writer for OutKick.
